prompt: Here's a flash-sale order-creation handler that's supposed to be idempotent: every incoming request carries an idempotency key, and Redis is meant to guarantee that concurrent duplicates of the same key produce exactly one order row. A recent refactor "cleaned up" the Redis guard by splitting what used to be a single atomic claim into a separate read step followed by a conditional write — and under real flash-sale load, two identical requests that land at the same instant both slip through and create two orders. Walk me through the code below: tell me exactly why splitting the check from the write reopened the race the idempotency key was meant to close, then describe how you'd restore a single atomic first-wins claim and correctly handle the caller that loses the race.
